choices.pr_choice: Remove exactly the fourth-ring data (R₄, E₄, σ₁₄, σ₄₁, σ₂₄, σ₄₂, σ₃₄, σ₄₃ and the 15 instance binders on them) from the file-wide variable block.
choices.excerpt: variable {R R₂ R₃ E E₂ E₃ F 𝓕 : Type*} [Semiring R] [Semiring R₂] [Semiring R₃]
choices.status_reason: The goal as the title and description paragraph 1 state it: the fourth-ring variables are carried by every declaration although only two use them.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief must name which variables are to leave the file-wide context, or the task cannot be stated; the title and description name them.
choices.consequence: Determines which declarations stop carrying the extra local instances, and so the performance gain.

choices.pr_choice: Keep the remaining variables of the block in their original relative order, reflowing only the line breaks.
choices.excerpt: [Module R E] [Module R₂ E₂] [Module R₃ E₃]
choices.status_reason: Every other declaration must keep its exact type (description paragraph 3), which fixes the order of the remaining binders.
choices.visibility_reason: Implied by the brief's requirement that every other declaration keep exactly its current type.
choices.consequence: Reordering the remaining binders would change the argument order of nearly every declaration in the file and break explicit (@) applications.

choices.pr_choice: Scope only the fourth ring; leave the third ring, F and 𝓕 and the other rarely used variables in the file-wide block.
choices.consequence: Scoping further variables could cut more typeclass-search work, at the cost of more local variable declarations and a larger diff.

choices.pr_choice: Give each theorem the fourth-ring data through a local section with its own variable command, rather than explicit binders in the theorem header (which an earlier revision used) or another scoping device.
choices.excerpt: variable {R₄ E₄ : Type*} [Semiring R₄] [SeminormedAddCommGroup E₄] [Module R₄ E₄]
choices.consequence: Fixes where the fourth-ring binders land in the theorems' argument order and how the context reads; explicit binders would keep the statement self-contained but make the headers long; the measured speed-up was reported for a different variant.

choices.pr_choice: Accept a new order of the implicit and instance arguments of the two theorems: the fourth-ring binders now follow all file-wide binders, with R₄ and E₄ and their structure instances first, then the homomorphisms, then the compatibility instances.
choices.excerpt: Only the order of their implicit and instance binders changes.
choices.consequence: Breaks any fully explicit (@) or positional use of the two theorems; the description reports none in Mathlib, but projects outside Mathlib are not covered.

choices.where: the two new local variable declarations
choices.pr_choice: Declare per theorem only the data it uses: for comp_assoc only σ₁₄, σ₂₄, σ₃₄ and three RingHomCompTriple instances (no inverse homomorphisms, no RingHomInvPair); for trans_assoc all six homomorphisms with six RingHomInvPair and six RingHomCompTriple instances.
choices.excerpt: {σ₁₄ : R →+* R₄} {σ₂₄ : R₂ →+* R₄} {σ₃₄ : R₃ →+* R₄}

choices.pr_choice: Leave both theorems where they are and wrap each in its own section, so the fourth-ring declarations are written twice rather than gathered once.
Add no comment explaining why the fourth-ring data is declared locally rather than in the file-wide block.
choices.consequence: Without a note, a later contributor may move the fourth-ring variables back into the file-wide block and undo the speed-up.

choices.pr_choice: Keep the names, statements, hypotheses, explicit arguments and generality of the two theorems unchanged.
choices.excerpt: The two statements do not change.
choices.status_reason: Description paragraph 3: the two theorems keep the same hypotheses and the same explicit arguments.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states it as a requirement to keep.
choices.consequence: Changing them would break the users of the two associativity lemmas.

choices.pr_choice: Confine the change to the one existing file that declares the variables.
choices.status_reason: The variables and their two users all live in this file.

feasibility_reason: The task is stated by naming the fourth-ring data in the existing file-wide block, its two existing users and the requirement that all types be kept, all of which the title and description give and which are the task itself. The consequential proposed choices stay withheld: the scoping device (local sections against explicit binders), the per-theorem variable sets, the duplication of the declarations, and the accepted reordering of the two theorems' implicit arguments. The last is posed in the brief as an open question without saying which way the PR went.
brief_omits: The timing figures (9.08 s to 7.10 s, the -26 % !bench), because the description ties the bench to an earlier revision that used explicit binders, which would reveal the design space the PR explored. The reference to #42214 as the same mechanism, since it points to the PR's design. The description's remark that Mathlib has no @-application of either theorem, since it is the PR's justification for reordering binders and would hint at the answer to the open question. The note that the PR was generated with Claude Code, which does not bear on the goal.
